name: Aider Polyglot
subtitle: 多编程语言的代码编辑与测试通过能力

officialDefinition.summary: 按自然语言要求修改现有代码并通过测试；题目来自 Exercism 的多语言练习。
officialDefinition.task: 在给定练习源码和自然语言要求后，模型通过 Aider 编辑流程提交代码修改，并接受该练习测试。

taskContract.input: 自然语言编程要求、练习现有源码及其单元测试。
taskContract.output: 练习文件的代码改动；任务是否成功按关联测试判定，榜单另记录编辑格式是否有效。
taskContract.environment: 官方建议使用 Docker 隔离执行生成代码；需同时记录 Aider/harness 版本、模型、edit format 和试验次数。

dataProfile.summary: 官方初版题库共 225 题，覆盖 C++、Go、Java、JavaScript、Python、Rust 六种语言。
scale: Aider 最初从六语言 Exercism 的 697 道练习中筛选出 225 题；这是初版选题过程。
splits: 官方未声明 train/dev/test split；题库按语言目录组织。
fields: 练习文件包含源码、自然语言任务说明及关联测试；官方没有定义统一 JSONL 行 schema。
files: polyglot-benchmark 仓库按 cpp/、go/、java/、javascript/、python/、rust/ 目录存储练习。

requirements: 题库公开于 Aider-AI/polyglot-benchmark；执行与统计 harness 位于 Aider 主仓库 benchmark/。

reusePolicy.license: 所选 Exercism C++、Go、JavaScript、Rust、Python track 官方 LICENSE 为 MIT；Aider README 明确练习来自这些 track，并按其开放许可使用。
reusePolicy.scope: 固定 Aider 提交中的所选作者练习指令文本，保留 Exercism 与具体作者署名；不镜像题面引用的第三方图片。
boundaries: 题目正文固定到 Aider 提交；各 track 的许可文件是本轮另行读取的版本，二者分别留档。

sampleAccess.reason: 5 条真实案例可在本站切换查看，原字段及数据入口保留。每条解析说明具体任务和取样范围；公开示例不代替完整题集。

metric.name: pass_rate_2
metric.description: Aider leaderboard 主排序量：配置的多次尝试中通过全部测试的任务比例；同时报告编辑格式有效率、成本等。结果依模型、prompt、edit format、尝试数和 harness commit 而变。

limitations.text: Exercism 六语言 track 的每道题及第三方素材许可需逐仓库、逐文件核对。
官方题库未声明稳定语义版本；比较结果前需固定题库与 harness commit。
leaderboard 的 pass_rate 受具体运行配置影响，不能只按 benchmark 名称横向比较。

sources.label: 具体公开案例的原始来源

researchNotes.text: 官方题库和 leaderboard 可公开访问，但题目来自不同 Exercism tracks，整套题库没有统一数据许可声明。未逐文件确认前不复制题目或测试；可链接官方题库。
本轮核对公开具体案例，定位 python/exercises/practice/wordy；正式训练/测试用途与本站展示范围不混用。
2026-10-19 真实记录补核：逐字段核对官方原始响应，本轮去重后新增 4 条，现有 5 条；保留原字段与值，并提供逐条中文解析。文件修订和 HF /rows 响应快照分别记录，不把另行观察的仓库 HEAD 当作 /rows 固定版本。
2026-10-19 全量补核结论：本轮新增4条、撤回0条；已采用的原始字段/连续源片段按证据逐项核对，分别配中文解析。可查看“Rust · 双桶量水步数”等案例；每条的附件缺口与取样范围单独说明。 展示记录1→5条；核验日期不是发布日期。

samples.title: C++ · 跨进制转换
samples.prompt: 需要把一个数的数字序列从源进制转换到目标进制、保持数值不变；原题特别提示自行实现转换。
samples.raw:
# Instructions

Convert a sequence of digits in one base, representing a number, into a sequence of digits in another base, representing the same number.

~~~~exercism/note
Try to implement the conversion yourself.
Do not use something else to perform the conversion for you.
~~~~

## About [Positional Notation][positional-notation]

In positional notation, a number in base **b** can be understood as a linear combination of powers of **b**.

The number 42, _in base 10_, means:

`(4 × 10¹) + (2 × 10⁰)`

The number 101010, _in base 2_, means:

`(1 × 2⁵) + (0 × 2⁴) + (1 × 2³) + (0 × 2²) + (1 × 2¹) + (0 × 2⁰)`

The number 1120, _in base 3_, means:

`(1 × 3³) + (1 × 3²) + (2 × 3¹) + (0 × 3⁰)`

_Yes. Those three numbers above are exactly the same. Congratulations!_

[positional-notation]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Positional_notation

samples.title: JavaScript · 棋盘皇后攻击关系
samples.prompt: 题面给出两枚皇后的位置，判断其是否同一行、列或对角线；示例采用8×8棋盘坐标。
samples.raw:
# Instructions

Given the position of two queens on a chess board, indicate whether or not they are positioned so that they can attack each other.

In the game of chess, a queen can attack pieces which are on the same row, column, or diagonal.

A chessboard can be represented by an 8 by 8 array.

So if you are told the white queen is at `c5` (zero-indexed at column 2, row 3) and the black queen at `f2` (zero-indexed at column 5, row 6), then you know that the set-up is like so:

![A chess board with two queens. Arrows emanating from the queen at c5 indicate possible directions of capture along file, rank and diagonal.](https://assets.exercism.org/images/exercises/queen-attack/queen-capture.svg)

You are also able to answer whether the queens can attack each other.
In this case, that answer would be yes, they can, because both pieces share a diagonal.

## Credit

The chessboard image was made by [habere-et-dispertire][habere-et-dispertire] using LaTeX and the [chessboard package][chessboard-package] by Ulrike Fischer.

[habere-et-dispertire]: https://exercism.org/profiles/habere-et-dispertire
[chessboard-package]: https://github.com/u-fischer/chessboard

samples.title: Go · 多地区货币台账重构
samples.prompt: 原任务是重构台账格式化器，输入涉及美国/荷兰地区格式与美元/欧元；重点是改写既有可运行代码而保持行为。
samples.raw:
# Instructions

Refactor a ledger printer.

The ledger exercise is a refactoring exercise.
There is code that prints a nicely formatted ledger, given a locale (American or Dutch) and a currency (US dollar or euro).
The code however is rather badly written, though (somewhat surprisingly) it consistently passes the test suite.

Rewrite this code.
Remember that in refactoring the trick is to make small steps that keep the tests passing.
That way you can always quickly go back to a working version.
Version control tools like git can help here as well.

Please keep a log of what changes you've made and make a comment on the exercise containing that log, this will help reviewers.

samples.title: Rust · 双桶量水步数
samples.prompt: 给定两个不同容量水桶、目标升数与先装满的桶，要求计算量出目标容量所需动作数；题面还约束每步倒水/倒空/装满及初始桶状态。
samples.raw:
# Instructions

Given two buckets of different size and which bucket to fill first, determine how many actions are required to measure an exact number of liters by strategically transferring fluid between the buckets.

There are some rules that your solution must follow:

- You can only do one action at a time.
- There are only 3 possible actions:
  1. Pouring one bucket into the other bucket until either:
     a) the first bucket is empty
     b) the second bucket is full
  2. Emptying a bucket and doing nothing to the other.
  3. Filling a bucket and doing nothing to the other.
- After an action, you may not arrive at a state where the initial starting bucket is empty and the other bucket is full.

Your program will take as input:

- the size of bucket one
- the size of bucket two
- the desired number of liters to reach
- which bucket to fill first, either bucket one or bucket two

Your program should determine:

- the total number of actions it should take to reach the desired number of liters, including the first fill of the starting bucket
- which bucket should end up with the desired number of liters - either bucket one or bucket two
- how many liters are left in the other bucket

Note: any time a change is made to either or both buckets counts as one (1) action.

Example:
Bucket one can hold up to 7 liters, and bucket two can hold up to 11 liters.
Let's say at a given step, bucket one is holding 7 liters and bucket two is holding 8 liters (7,8).
If you empty bucket one and make no change to bucket two, leaving you with 0 liters and 8 liters respectively (0,8), that counts as one action.
Instead, if you had poured from bucket one into bucket two until bucket two was full, resulting in 4 liters in bucket one and 11 liters in bucket two (4,11), that would also only count as one action.

Another Example:
Bucket one can hold 3 liters, and bucket two can hold up to 5 liters.
You are told you must start with bucket one.
So your first action is to fill bucket one.
You choose to empty bucket one for your second action.
For your third action, you may not fill bucket two, because this violates the third rule -- you may not end up in a state after any action where the starting bucket is empty and the other bucket is full.

Written with <3 at [Fullstack Academy][fullstack] by Lindsay Levine.

[fullstack]: https://www.fullstackacademy.com/
